neighbours.label: preposition (for / of / to) that links a getting-ready or anticipation phrase to an upcoming event (prepare for, ahead of, in advance of, the run-up to)
fire: The choir has been rehearsing every night as it prepares for the Christmas concert.
Shops stocked up on candles in advance of the holiday weekend.
The swimmers are training hard for the national trials in June.
Security was tightened across the city ahead of the summit.
Families cleaned their houses in preparation for the New Year festival.
The runners are gearing up for the marathon on Sunday.
Volunteers decorated the hall in the days leading up to the graduation ceremony.
The students are revising late into the night as they get ready for their finals.
quiet: The choir has been praised every night for its Christmas concert.
Shops ran out of candles because of the holiday weekend.
The swimmers were thanked for their work at the national trials in June.
Security was a major topic of the summit.
Families cleaned their houses with a mixture of vinegar and water.
The runners were grateful for the water on Sunday.
Volunteers decorated the hall with photos of the graduation ceremony.
The students are known for their kindness to new arrivals.

notes: Card: ' for', ' of' after 'prepare', 'ahead', 'gearing up', 'in advance', 'train'. Probes: 'getting ready for' 0.52, 'Ahead of the election' 0.48, 'run-up to' 0.49, 'exam is coming soon' 0.67; 'a present for her brother' 0.02, 'picture of the mountain' 0.01, 'bracing for' 0.16.
